nonprofit-executive.title: Black foundation executives organized a professional association
nonprofit-executive.description: The Association of Black Foundation Executives began as a volunteer network. It gave Black professionals in philanthropy a collective voice in decisions about foundation leadership and investment in Black communities.
nonprofit-executive.sourceTitle: ABFE · About us and organizational history

nonprofit-executive.title: A leadership program included nonprofit executives
nonprofit-executive.description: The African American Leadership Family founded the Masters Series for Distinguished Leaders. Through the Skinner Leadership Institute, nonprofit leaders could learn alongside executives from business and government.
nonprofit-executive.sourceTitle: Skinner Leadership Institute · Masters Series for Distinguished Leaders

elected-official.title: Black legislators entered both chambers of Congress
elected-official.description: During Reconstruction, Mississippi sent a Black senator to Washington and South Carolina elected a Black representative. These were the first Black members to serve in the U.S. Congress.
elected-official.sourceTitle: U.S. House of Representatives · Black Americans in Congress

elected-official.title: Federal law challenged barriers to Black voting
elected-official.description: Congress passed the Voting Rights Act. It suspended literacy tests and authorized federal voter-registration examiners in certain jurisdictions with a history of discrimination. Those changes broadened access to the electorate that chooses public officials.
elected-official.sourceTitle: National Archives · Congress and the Voting Rights Act of 1965

pastor.title: Black congregations organized an independent denomination
pastor.description: Black Methodist congregations met in Philadelphia and formed the African Methodist Episcopal Church. They established their own church leadership and consecrated the denomination’s first bishop.
pastor.sourceTitle: Library of Congress · Proceedings of the AME Church General Conference, historical chronology

pastor.title: Four seminaries joined to train clergy
pastor.description: Four seminaries chartered the Interdenominational Theological Center in Atlanta. The shared graduate school gave Black church traditions a common setting for theological education.

military-officer.title: Fort Des Moines trained and commissioned Black officers
military-officer.description: After advocacy from the NAACP and others, the U.S. Army chose Fort Des Moines to train Black officer candidates. Graduates received commissions in October for service in a segregated Army.
military-officer.sourceTitle: National Park Service · Fort Des Moines: A Series of Firsts in Wartime Service

military-officer.title: An executive order directed the armed services to expand equal opportunity
military-officer.description: Executive Order 9981 made equal treatment and opportunity regardless of race a policy across the U.S. armed services. It created a committee to review military rules and practices. Implementation took place over time.
military-officer.sourceTitle: National Archives · Executive Order 9981, text of the order

police-officer.title: Atlanta placed its first Black police officers on duty
police-officer.description: The Atlanta Police Department assigned its first Black officers to Auburn Avenue. This was a documented opening in one city’s police force.
police-officer.sourceTitle: Atlanta Police Department · History of the APD

police-officer.title: Black police officers in St. Louis organized against discrimination
police-officer.description: African American police officers founded the Ethical Society of Police to challenge racial discrimination. The organization gave officers a way to advocate collectively for fair treatment within policing.
police-officer.sourceTitle: Ethical Society of Police · Organizational history

electrician.title: Edward Mays helps select Local 3 apprentices
electrician.description: Edward Mays, a Black electrician who had completed the union’s apprenticeship, helped select new apprentices for Local 3 in New York City. The local recruited through civil rights groups and vocational schools.
electrician.sourceTitle: Marshall and Briggs · Apprenticeship study, pp. 6–7

electrician.title: The revised Philadelphia Plan included electrical workers
electrician.description: Federal contract officials introduced hiring requirements for covered construction contracts in the Philadelphia area. Electrical work was among the trades targeted because minority workers had been excluded.
electrician.sourceTitle: U.S. Commission on Civil Rights · Federal Civil Rights Enforcement Effort, Philadelphia Plan

electrician.title: Electrical workers formed a caucus for representation inside their union
electrician.description: Black and Hispanic delegates at the International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers convention formed the Electrical Workers Minority Caucus. They organized to challenge unequal representation and treatment within the union.

corporate-executive.title: Black executives formed the Executive Leadership Council
corporate-executive.description: Corporate executives created a professional network to support one another and develop routes into senior business leadership. The council’s history traces its beginnings to an effort to support a historically Black college.

corporate-executive.title: The council created Strengthening the Pipeline
corporate-executive.description: Black professionals nominated by council members or employers could receive coaching, mentoring and training for executive responsibilities. The program offered a route to prepare for advancement within a company.
corporate-executive.sourceTitle: Center for Talent Innovation and Executive Leadership Council · Being Black in Corporate America, program profile

entrepreneur.title: Black business owners built a national trade association
entrepreneur.description: The National Negro Business League began in Boston. Its local chapters brought Black business owners and professionals together to exchange knowledge and promote Black enterprise.

entrepreneur.title: A federal office built a business support network
entrepreneur.description: The Office of Minority Business Enterprise established a national network of business development organizations and provided seed funding to minority business associations. Black-owned firms were part of the broader constituency it served.
entrepreneur.sourceTitle: Minority Business Development Agency · History, 1973 milestone

pro-athlete.title: Black newspapers pressed the Rams to open their roster
pro-athlete.description: When the Rams sought dates at the Los Angeles Coliseum, Black newspaper editors challenged the team’s exclusion of Black players. The Coliseum Commission adopted a nondiscrimination rule for professional teams using the venue. That spring the Rams signed two Black players.
pro-athlete.sourceTitle: Los Angeles Public Library · Los Angeles and the reintegration of the NFL

pro-athlete.title: NBA teams began integrating their rosters
pro-athlete.description: The Boston Celtics drafted a Black player, the New York Knicks signed one, and the Washington Capitols fielded one in a regular-season game. Together those decisions opened NBA team rosters to Black players.
pro-athlete.sourceTitle: National Basketball Association · The league’s first integration season

musician.title: Black musicians pressed for one Los Angeles union
musician.description: Members of the predominantly Black musicians’ Local 767 brought a formal proposal to the board of Local 47. They sought a single musicians’ local in a city where studio work and union representation had been segregated.
musician.sourceTitle: American Federation of Musicians Local 47 · The story of amalgamation

musician.title: The two Los Angeles musicians’ locals merged
musician.description: Local 767 and Local 47 became one union. Black musicians could participate in the same local that represented many of the city’s studio musicians.
musician.sourceTitle: American Federation of Musicians Local 47 · Our history
